title: Design a Durable Webhook Delivery Platform
prompt: Design a platform where tenants register multiple callback subscriptions for event types. Every matching subscription receives a signed at-least-once HTTP delivery, with retries, rate limits, replay, and delivery history. Cover source-event durability, fan-out, endpoint security, backoff, dead letters, and operational isolation.

response.placeholder: Make a subscription—not an event type—the delivery unit. Explain what survives a retry or endpoint outage.
response.reference_answer:
## Subscription model
A subscription contains tenant, event type, endpoint version, secret reference, enablement state, and subscription ID. One event may create many delivery tasks; do not overwrite one URL per event type.

## Durable fan-out
Transactionally append the source event and outbox record, then materialize one idempotent delivery task per matching subscription. Workers sign a delivery ID and payload version, persist attempts before/after HTTP, and accept an endpoint acknowledgement as only one attempt outcome. External HTTP cannot be exactly once.

## Retries and safety
Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter, endpoint and host concurrency limits, circuit breaking, DLQ, and operator replay. Defend against SSRF with URL validation, DNS/IP policy, redirect policy, payload limits, and secret rotation. Cache subscription lookup by version and invalidate on edits.

## Operations
Track fan-out lag, endpoint failures, retry age, DLQ size, delivery success by tenant, and abusive destinations.

## Progressive Hints
1. A durable event and a delivery attempt are different records.
2. A retry must preserve delivery identity.
3. Exactly-once HTTP is not a realistic promise.
